question: Can a UD harmonic translation/source port restrict the remaining signed friction and load response once conventional honeycomb, moire, contact and material-bath effects are fixed?
assumptions: Seven-cell honeycomb cellular torus uses unit-edge cochain metric for the exact carrier.
Physical relative translation is mapped to its two harmonic 1-cochains; this identification is a hypothesis.
Weighted incidence source contrast S(w)=M^T W B1^T is a candidate physical source rule, not established graphite atomistics.
Internal stiffness K is positive and passive D_h is nonnegative for the conditional low-frequency response.
Baseline PES, contact, force estimator, and damping need independent calibration before held-out prediction.
physical_mapping: Uncalibrated harmonic translation and material source map; no native-to-physical damping or force coefficient; mainline physical promotion 0.
target_exposure: Angles 21.8 and 38.2 degrees and weak load response were known before model selection; DFT first-shell and archive data used in development; no held-out experimental force table available.
fitted_choices: Ordinary (2,1) coincidence selected after angle exposure
KC plus plate parameters and first-shell DFT fits are exploratory conventional material models
Illustrative off-line high-harmonic epsilon=-0.2 U1 is a falsification contrast, not a material fit
baseline: Conventional honeycomb/moire coincidence, full two-dimensional material PES, contact and independently measured bath loss; same-source KC and vdW-DF3 discrepancy retained.
result: EXACT theta=acos(13/14), complement 60-theta, b1=2, uniform-weight S=0. CONDITIONAL Gamma_add=C K^-1 D_h K^-1 C^T. NUMERICAL source-replayed ideal static ratio 2.104. OPEN signed kinetic force and pressure residual.
next_discriminant: Complete five off-line QE probes plus regularity/error bounds, independently calibrate response and source weights, freeze signed paired-angle residual and derivative, then test held-out force data.
